summary: Two Leadville men in their 30s backcountry skiing in the Sleeping Indian area triggered an avalanche in a northeast-facing chute near the Mt. Arkansas summit (~13,700 ft) around 9:30am; one was partially buried and extricated by the C-RAD team with injuries requiring a Flight for Life extraction to St. Anthony Hospital in Denver, while the second was cold but uninjured; both were off the mountain by about 2pm
location: Sleeping Indian area, NE-facing chute near Mt. Arkansas summit, Mosquito Range
responding_agency: Lake County SAR, Colorado Rapid Avalanche Deployment (C-RAD) team from Arapahoe Basin, Flight for Life
notes: Article published 2018-03-09; incident occurred Wednesday 2018-03-07 per article (matches "Wednesday's mission"); original reporting by Leadville Today (leadvilletoday.com) | Run 173: CAIC classic 2017-18 table (opened this run) lists 1 tourer caught, partially buried, injured — row keeps victims=2 per the SnowBrains account of the two involved tourers.
